newsitem.title: USA: Argentina soy crop dips to 13.25 mln T--US attache.
newsitem.headline: Argentina soy crop dips to 13.25 mln T--US attache.

text.p: The Argentine soybean crop probably will total 13.25 million tonnes, down 250,000 tonnes due to dry weather, the U.S. agricutural attache in Buenos Aries said in a report released Monday.
The U.S. Agriculture Department has forecast the Argentine crop at 13.50 million tonnes. It will update its forecast on Friday in its monthly World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates report.
Recent rainfall has relieved drought conditions, the attache said, but rain was too late for some areas and was scattered in others so yields would be variable.
"Based on the aforementioned conditions, post recommends that the production (estimate) be reduced from 13.5 million tonnes to 13.25 million tonnes," the attache wrote.

"Soybean harvest has begun in Argentina, with about two percent completed as of March 21. Conditions have been generally favorable, with the notable exception of significant areas of Cordoba province and the northeast of Buenos Aires where first crop beans were seriously affected.

"Recent rainfall did provide some relief to drought conditions, especially for second crop, but in other areas proved to be too late to arrest the downturn in potential. Further, the rain that did fall was scattered, which is expected to result in variable yields."
